description: A donut where one slice is enlarged and outlined with an outer arc to highlight it.
overview: Uses `PieChart` with one `Pie` (`innerRadius="50%"`, `outerRadius="78%"`, `strokeWidth={0}`) and a `shape` render function. For the slice whose index equals `ACTIVE`, it returns two `Sector` elements: the slice extended by 10 pixels and a thin arc 13 to 16 pixels beyond the original radius; other slices render a plain `Sector`. `chartData` holds five `{ device, users, fill }` records, where each `fill` is `var(--color-<device>)`. `chartConfig` defines `users` (label only) plus `phone`, `laptop`, `tablet`, `watch` and `other` colored `var(--blue)`, `var(--teal)`, `var(--indigo)`, `var(--orange)` and `var(--gray)`. The tooltip uses `ChartTooltipContent` with `hideLabel` and `nameKey="device"`.
usage: Replace `chartData` with your categories, giving each record a `fill` of `var(--color-<key>)`, and add a matching `chartConfig` entry with `label` and `color` for every key. Keep `dataKey` and `nameKey` on `Pie` pointed at your value and category fields, and update the tooltip's `nameKey` if you rename the category field. Set `ACTIVE` to the index of the slice to highlight, or replace it with a value from `React.useState` to drive the highlight from user input. Change the pixel offsets inside `shape` to adjust how far the slice and ring extend.
notes: The highlight is static: `ACTIVE` is a constant, so it doesn't follow hover. `accessibilityLayer` is set on `PieChart`, so the chart is focusable and arrow keys move between slices.
